data.claim: Commits on the base whose subject is 'merge <id>:' or '<id>:' and that touch the item's globs identify the item's change; fail closed otherwise
data.falsifier: A cited commit that touches only docs while the item's code landed elsewhere would wrongly select the doc pipeline
data.mechanism: git log --first-parent --grep; changed_paths per cited commit; union; plus explicit verified --landed range
data.probe: git log main --grep='merge RM-long-ops-research:' on the real repo shows a single cited commit 0982ed48d touching docs only
data.question: Can an item's change be derived reliably when its work landed outside ddflow merge?

chunk_findings.detail: When a worktree/branch exists but `out` is empty (the existing comment explicitly calls out “a branch already merged into its base”), the function still executes `return sorted(out) if out else None` and never reaches the new `return LD.cited_paths(repo, it, base)` fallback. That means an item whose branch was landed via a plain git merge or mixed commit—so `git diff` against `base` is empty—still gets `changed_paths()` == `None`, `diff_is_docs_only` remains false, and the full task pipeline is applied to a docs-only item. Example input: item `SU-decision-...` has branch `feature-decision` already merged into `base=main`; `out == []`; the new cited-commit fallback is skipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:changed_paths

chunk_findings.detail: The `git log` command uses `--first-parent`, so it only walks the first-parent chain from `base`. A cited commit on a side branch that landed via a normal non-fast-forward merge is reachable from `base` and is precisely the "plain git merge" case this file says it covers, but it is omitted. Concrete failure: commit `C` on `feature` has subject `B9eb92adafe: add doc` and touches `docs/decision.md`; `main` merges `feature` with merge commit `M` whose subject is `"Merge branch 'feature'"`. `cited_ranges(repo, item, "main")` returns `[]`, so `cited_paths` returns `None` and the full task pipeline is still applied to a docs-only decision item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/landed.py: cited_ranges

chunk_findings.detail: A cited commit that cannot be diffed is silently omitted instead of forcing `cited_paths` to return `None`. For a cited root commit, `%P` is empty, so `if not first or not _cites(...): continue` discards it even though its subject cites the item. If a later cited commit verifiably changes only docs, `cited_paths` still returns that docs path rather than `None`. Concrete input: base has a root commit `B9: initial work` touching `src/code.py` and `docs/decision.md`, and a later commit `B9: add decision` touching only `docs/decision.md`; the root commit is dropped, `cited_paths` returns `docs/decision.md`, and `diff_is_docs_only` skips the full task pipeline despite a cited commit that touched code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/landed.py:cited_ranges

chunk_findings.detail: `cited_ranges` matches commits across all of `base` by the human-chosen `item.id` alone. [D-B191-item-ids-accepted] says the same id can be reused via `--readd` after removal, but the function has no notion of the current item's lifetime or definition. A removed item's old nil-cited docs commit remains in `base`; after `B9` is readded with overlapping declared globs and no branch, that old commit is returned as the new item's landing, so `cited_paths`/`diff_is_docs_only` can classify the unlanded new item as docs-only.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/landed.py:cited_ranges

chunk_findings.detail: The early full-scope return still runs the whole suite for the exact item this change is meant to fix. For a docs-only decision item whose effective pipeline omits the CI gate, `_ci_not_passed_here` sees `"ci" not in _pipeline(cfg, it, tree)` and returns the "no ci gate..." reason; line 108 then returns `Scope("full", why, needs_ci=False)`. A `Scope("full")` still makes the test runner execute the full suite, so required unit_tests still apply to a docs-only item (B9eb92adafe), even though the pipeline was reduced. The docs-only effective pipeline should suppress this fallback; as written it only changes the `needs_ci` flag.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:108

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression tests only create default-kind `task` items via `_unmerged_task` (`run_cli(repo, "task", "add", "T1", ...)` with no `--kind`). The intent explicitly names `research`-kind items (B75d2b12ff1) as still excluded from docs-only and says to include kind research. No test constructs a `kind="research"` item with a docs-only cited commit, and the pre-existing assertion at line 147 still expects `not diff_is_docs_only(it, cfg, ["docs/x.md"])`. Thus a version that leaves `diff_is_docs_only` returning False for `kind != "task"` — the reported bug — still passes all newly added tests, or, if the fix does change `diff_is_docs_only` for research, that unchanged assertion fails and breaks the suite.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_docs_only_task_pipeline.py:147

chunk_findings.detail: `_landed_fields` validates `--landed` against `it.base` (or the default base) before `plan_edit` applies the same update's `edit.base`. If a single update changes `base` and sets `landed`, the landed commit is checked against the outgoing base. Concretely: item has `base=main` and no landed range; commit `c` is on `main` but not on `release/1`; `update` with `base=release/1` and `landed=c` passes `LD.check` against `main`, then records `base=release/1` and `landed_after=c`, leaving the item with a landed commit that is not on its base. The check should use `edit.base` when provided, since that is the post-update base being recorded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items.py:_landed_fields

chunk_findings.detail: The change delegates the docs-only pipeline decision to the existing `docsonly.pipeline_by_diff`, but the manifest contains no modification to `ddflow/services/docsonly.py`, so the pre-existing `diff_is_docs_only` guard that rejects `item.kind != 'task'` remains. As a result, a research item (`RM-*`/`RV-*`) whose only changed path is a doc file still receives the full declared research pipeline. Example: an item `RM-decision-1` with only `docs/decision.md` in `changed_paths(repo, item)` calls `effective_pipeline(repo, cfg, item)`; `pipeline_by_diff` returns `(base, False)` because the item kind is not `task`, so `report.py` and other callers of this new choke point still apply the full research/testing pipeline, leaving the stated B75d2b12ff1 bug unresolved.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/pipeline_diff.py:20 effective_pipeline

chunk_findings.detail: The stated fix for B9eb92adafe requires `diff_is_docs_only` to include kind `"research"`, but the existing assertion `assert not diff_is_docs_only(it, cfg, ["docs/x.md"])` for `Item(id="X", kind="research", title="t", globs=["docs/x.md"])` is left unchanged. Given the intended change, running this regression test will hit that assertion and fail; the test must be updated or removed, and no new test covers a cited docs-only `research` item.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_docs_only_task_pipeline.py:147

chunk_findings.detail: Previously reported still holds: `cited_ranges` selects commits by `item.id` alone, but the new `--since=created_at-2min` window does not implement the lifetime rule in [D-B191-item-ids-accepted]. Concrete reproduction allowed by that rule: item `B9` is added, a docs-only commit citing `B9` is made, the item is removed, and `B9` is immediately re-added (within 2 minutes via `--readd`). The new item's `created_at` is the re-add time, so `--since=created_at-2min` still includes the old removed item's cited docs-only commit. `cited_paths` then returns that docs file, `diff_is_docs_only` classifies the new `B9` as docs-only, and required unit tests are skipped. The ID lifetime is still not checked against the new item's definition, and there is no dedicated regression test for this allowed immediate re-add case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/landed.py:cited_ranges

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier [D-B191-item-ids-accepted] lifetime issue is only narrowed, not answered. `_since` is a commit-date cutoff, not an actual item-definition/lifetime boundary, so a `--readd` within two minutes still credits the prior item's commit. Input: an old B9 cited commit with committer date `10:00` touching `docs/old.md`; remove B9 and `--readd` at `10:01`. `_since(item.created_at)` computes `09:59`, so `git log --since=09:59` still selects the old commit and `cited_paths` can classify the unlanded new item as docs-only. The probe only shows older commits are excluded; it does not cover this two-minute reuse window.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/landed.py:cited_ranges

chunk_findings.detail: The cited_ranges fix only narrows by `--since=created_at-2min`, not by the current item's lifetime or definition. An old removed item's docs-only commit can still be returned for a readded id when the removal/readd happens within that two-minute window. Concrete input: old `B9` item has docs-only commit `abc123` at time T; at T+30s the user removes and readds `B9`. The new item's `created_at` is T+30s, so the `--since=T-1m30s` range still includes `abc123`. `cited_ranges` then returns that old item's landing for the new item, so `changed_paths`/`diff_is_docs_only` can classify the unlanded new item as docs-only based on a removed lifetime, violating [D-B191-item-ids-accepted]. The probe's two-minute mitigation does not answer this, so the finding still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/landed.py:cited_ranges

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 2 still holds. The triage says `cited_ranges` now uses `--since=created_at-2min`, but that is only a time window, not a lifetime boundary. Under [D-B191-item-ids-accepted] the same id may be removed and `--readd` immediately. Concrete input: an old cited docs commit is made at time t0, the item is removed at t0+1s, and the same id is readded at t0+10s. The new item’s `created_at` is t0+10s, so `--since=t0-1m50s` still includes the old commit. `cited_ranges` credits the new, unlanded item with that old commit, classifies it docs-only, and skips required gates. The added tests do not exercise this fast-readd path, so the time-window mitigation does not fully fix the bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/landed.py:cited_ranges

chunk_findings.detail: A root commit is an already-landed commit, but `parse` refuses `--landed <root-sha>` as having no parent and tells the user to give `<before>..<after>`. The only possible `before` for a root commit is `_EMPTY_TREE`, but `check` rejects that because `git merge-base --is-ancestor` requires commits and `_EMPTY_TREE` is a tree, not a commit. Concrete scenario: `c` is the root commit on `main` with subject `SU-decision: add doc`; `ddflow update SU-decision --landed c` returns "has no parent to diff against", and `--landed 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904..c` returns "4b825dc642cb is not an ancestor of main". So a root docs landing outside `ddflow merge` cannot be attached via `--landed`, even though `cited_ranges` handles root commits with `_EMPTY_TREE`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/landed.py parse/_EMPTY_TREE/check

chunk_findings.detail: The previous base-specific refutation does not cover the editable `globs` field: `queue.py:50` adds `landed` to the same `ItemEdit` constructor that can also change the item's globs, and `--landed` is described as “verified as ancestors of the base touching the item's globs.” `_landed_fields` reads the current item before `plan_edit` merges the same update’s other fields, so the touch check can be wrong for a one-step update. Concretely: an item has `globs=["src/*.py"]` and no landed record; commit `c` on the base touches only `docs/decision.md`; the user runs an update with `--globs 'docs/*.md' --landed c`. This should be valid for the globs being set, but `_landed_fields` checks `c` against the outgoing `src/*.py` globs and refuses it. The validation must be performed against the post-edit item/globs, not the outgoing item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items.py:_landed_fields

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test for B4da2fc502b never invokes any diffless production caller. It imports `effective_pipeline` and calls it directly, then asserts `G.pipeline_for` still returns the task pipeline. Reverting every actual caller (`report.py`, `report_gates.py`, `testscope.py`, `verify.py`, `mergequeue_run.py`) back to `G.pipeline_for` would leave this test passing, even though the original bug would be fully reintroduced. The test therefore does not detect the bug it claims to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_docs_only_task_pipeline.py:test_diffless_callers_share_the_pipeline_from_the_diff
